entries.grounds: mutant_view confirms `present = sum(1 for p in folder.glob('*.json') if p.is_file() and _NAME.fullmatch(p.name))` -> `... if p.is_file() or _NAME.fullmatch(p.name)`. The author's grounds claim a verify verdict flip (spurious REFUTED, or masked -> 'false VERIFIED'). DISPROVEN by direct reproduction against the snapshot: directory {S1.1.p1.json (valid), stray.json}: with written=1 ORIGINAL problems=['...stray.json is not a file this release writes'] (no count problem); MUTANT problems=[same, 'RUN.json states 1 written, the directory holds 2']. With written=2 ORIGINAL=[stray-problem, 'holds 1']; MUTANT=[stray-problem only]. In EVERY case the verdict is REFUTED either way, because the only file that makes `present` diverge (a stray real .json, or a _NAME-named non-file i.e. a directory) is INDEPENDENTLY a main-loop problem: a stray *.json -> 'is not a file this release writes' (L281-282) AND an evidence_manifest mismatch (run.py:429 globs *.json, so stray.json is in `fresh` but not `stored`); a _NAME-named directory -> read fails -> 'is not a probe observation' (L286-289). So the mutant never emits 'NO problem'/false VERIFIED. It only changes the presence/content of the operator-read count-mismatch MESSAGE, which no program parses and which is always accompanied by an independent true problem. The count check is also a redundant second defense for removal (the _run test says 'refuted by the manifest AND by the count'). By the audit's own dividing line (REFUTED only where the verify verdict can flip), this is AUDITED, not test-owed. Survives both kill files (unit 59 OK, run 25 OK).
